cards.title: Poisson resonance number variance

checks.reason: The paper identifies the dashed line as Poisson-distributed resonances and defines the interval mean count.
A Poisson count has equal mean and variance by its probability-generating function.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate Sigma2=L on the declared mean-count grid.

cards.title: GOE number variance from the two-level cluster function

checks.reason: The caption and text require the Wigner-Dyson/GOE number-variance comparator.
Integrating the connected two-level correlation over an interval gives the count-variance identity.
The result begins at zero, has unit initial slope, and grows logarithmically rather than linearly at large L.

cards.numerical_form: Quadrature of the standard unfolded GOE cluster function with a small-s series at the removable singularity.
open_questions: The paper does not state whether its plotted Wigner-Dyson variance uses exact GOE correlations or a finite random-matrix sample; both will be cross-checked.

cards.title: Poisson and Wigner nearest-neighbor spacing laws
cards.latex: P_{\rm P}(s)=e^{-s},\qquad P_{\rm W}(s)=\frac{\pi s}{2}e^{-\pi s^2/4}

checks.reason: Fig. 2(b) names Poisson and Wigner-Dyson distributions for normalized spacings.
Both densities integrate to one and have unit mean spacing.
Poisson permits P(0)=1 while the Wigner surmise has linear level repulsion.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate both normalized densities on a common nonnegative spacing grid.

cards.title: Quadratic excess ion energy

source_refs.value: Main energy-scaling equation and Appendix tuning section

cards.latex: E_{\rm ion}=E_{\min}+\Delta E_{\rm ion}=E_{\min}+\alpha\mathcal E_{\rm dc}^2

checks.reason: The equation and alpha_sim=10(1) mK/(V/m)^2 are printed in the main text and appendix.
alpha times electric-field squared has energy units.
At compensated field the excess term vanishes and Eion=Emin.

cards.numerical_form: Report ensemble median kinetic energy and fit it against field squared without a linear term.
open_questions: The paper withholds the numerical MD arrays and convergence settings.

cards.title: Isolated-ion excess-micromotion coefficient

checks.reason: The appendix prints the expression and alpha_theo,y=16.4(10) mK/(V/m)^2.
The squared driven-velocity response divided by mass gives energy per field squared.
The isolated-ion prediction exceeds the interacting median coefficient, matching the stated 60 percent difference.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate the printed expression when complete Mathieu parameters are supplied; otherwise preserve the printed value as a cross-check only.
open_questions: The exact a_y and q_y used for the quoted number are not printed.

cards.title: Independent atom-ion collision update

source_refs.value: Appendix: Tuning the ion excess kinetic energy

cards.latex: \mathbf V=\frac{m_i\mathbf v_i+m_a\mathbf v_a}{m_i+m_a},\quad \mathbf v_i'=\mathbf V+\frac{m_a}{m_i+m_a}\,R(\mathbf v_i-\mathbf v_a)

checks.reason: The appendix requires 3D scattering, thermal atoms, radial rf drive, repeated collisions, and a steady-state median.
The isotropic COM-frame rotation conserves two-body momentum and kinetic energy exactly for each elastic collision.
With zero driven micromotion repeated collisions cool toward the thermal bath; radial drive creates anisotropic heavy tails.

cards.numerical_form: Event-driven 3D Langevin-collision chain with random rf phase, thermal Li velocities, isotropic COM scattering, and explicit checkpointable ensembles.
open_questions: C6, launch radius, exact Mathieu parameters, collision timing law, and author trajectory count are not printed; the independent event model is reconstructed rather than paper exact.

cards.title: Static field to harmonic displacement

source_refs.value: Main Fig. 4 displacement axis and Appendix rf-confinement discussion

checks.reason: The paper uses a dc field to displace a singly charged ion and prints the radial secular frequencies.
Force balance eE=m omega^2 y gives the mapping.
Electric force divided by harmonic stiffness has length units.

cards.numerical_form: Map between the lower displacement axis and upper electric-field/energy axes using the printed ion mass and secular frequency.
open_questions: The plotted radial direction is treated as the printed approximately 66 kHz confinement.

cards.title: Gaussian atomic density profile

checks.reason: The text prints sigma, FWHM, and center offset and identifies the solid line as Gaussian.
2 sqrt(2 ln 2) sigma gives 19.31 micrometers, consistent with the printed 19.4(8).
The profile is represented as n/n0, so no unpublished absolute marker normalization is required.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate the normalized Gaussian on a displacement grid and keep n0 as a separately declared physical parameter for loss rates.
open_questions: The exact peak density during Fig. 4 is not tabulated; the typical 5e11 cm^-3 value is declared as reconstructed when used.

cards.title: Classical three-body recombination survival

source_refs.value: Appendix: Classical description of three-body recombination loss

cards.latex: \gamma_l=k_3n^2(E_0+\Delta E_{\rm ion})^{-3/4},\qquad P_{\rm surv}=e^{-\gamma_l t_{\rm int}}

checks.reason: The appendix prints the loss law, E0=4.5(8) mK times 3/2 kB, and k3 at 10 mK; the methods print exponential survival.
The temperature-normalized k3 convention times density squared gives an inverse time.
Loss weakens as E^-3/4 at high energy and vanishes with density or interaction time.

cards.numerical_form: Use the quoted k3 normalization at 10 mK, local Gaussian density, E0, and 200 ms interaction to generate the classical branch.
open_questions: The figure-specific peak density is not printed, so absolute survival remains reconstructed while the scaling is fixed.

cards.title: Dimensionless polarization-potential radial equation

source_refs.value: Quantum recombination model and Appendix Fig. 8

checks.reason: The paper specifies the long-range charge-induced-dipole 1/R^4 interaction and E_s=8.8 microkelvin.
Scaling the -C4/r^4 radial Schrodinger equation by R*=sqrt(2 mu C4/hbar^2) gives the stated dimensionless form.
At large x the equation reduces to free spherical waves; at small x the attractive 1/x^4 term dominates.

cards.numerical_form: Integrate the complex radial equation from an incoming absorbing WKB boundary to an asymptotic matching radius.

cards.title: Partial-wave barrier energies

checks.reason: Appendix Fig. 8 marks the partial-wave barrier heights where coupling saturates.
Maximizing l(l+1)/x^2-1/x^4 gives x_b^2=2/[l(l+1)] and barrier [l(l+1)]^2/4.
The formula yields 1, 9, and 36 E_s for p, d, and f waves.

cards.numerical_form: Generate barrier guides directly from l without fitting the source figure.

cards.title: Universal short-range capture probability

source_refs.value: Quantum defect function C^-2(k), Appendix Fig. 8

checks.reason: The paper defines Gamma(k)=Gamma_m C_l^-2(k), threshold k^(2l+1), and saturation to unity.
An incoming-only short-range boundary makes lost flux 1-|S|^2 and therefore constrains the coupling to [0,1].
Independent log-log solutions recover k^(2l+1) at threshold and approach unity above the barrier.

cards.numerical_form: Match the propagated solution and derivative to incoming/outgoing Riccati-Hankel waves and compute flux loss.
open_questions: The paper withholds its exact quantum-defect numerical implementation and energy grid.

cards.title: Universal atom-dimer Langevin rate

source_refs.value: Quantum recombination model paragraph on K(k)

checks.reason: The paper states that K(k) is the parameter-free universal quantum-Langevin atom-molecule reaction rate.
Velocity times partial-wave loss cross section has volume-per-time units.
The s-wave contribution tends to the universal low-energy constant while higher waves turn on near their barriers.

cards.numerical_form: Sum independently computed capture probabilities with degeneracy and multiply by relative velocity.
open_questions: The atom-dimer polarization scale is not printed; the dimensionless energy dependence is fixed while its absolute scale is declared reconstructed.

cards.title: Resonant recombination cross section

checks.reason: The cross section is printed verbatim in the main text.
The Lorentzian rate ratio is dimensionless and pi/k^2 supplies area.
The cross section vanishes if either dimer formation or secondary reaction is turned off and is Lorentzian in detuning.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate with Gamma=Gamma_m C_l^-2, universal K, local density, and magnetic detuning.

cards.title: Magnetic detuning of the dimer state

source_refs.value: Definition below the recombination cross section

checks.reason: The paper prints the definition and reports delta mu=1.86 MHz/G for the s-wave fit and 0.35 MHz/G for the f-wave model.
Relative magnetic moment in frequency per field times field detuning gives frequency/energy detuning.
At B=B_res the bare detuning vanishes.

cards.numerical_form: Convert magnetic-field grids to angular-frequency detuning using the declared delta-mu convention.
open_questions: The f-wave short-range coupling Gamma_m and zero-energy bare B_res are not printed and must be reconstructed for qualitative spectra.

cards.title: Three-body relative kinetic energy and velocity averaging

source_refs.value: Quantum model averaging paragraph and MD appendix

cards.latex: E_{\rm rel}=\sum_{j=1}^3\frac{m_j}{2}|\mathbf v_j-\mathbf V_{\rm cm}|^2,\quad \langle\gamma\rangle=\mathbb E[\sigma(k)nv]

checks.reason: The paper requires averaging over nonthermal ion and thermal atom velocity distributions in the three-body relative frame.
Subtracting the center-of-mass velocity exactly separates translational and internal kinetic energy.
For equal velocities the relative energy vanishes; a zero-temperature heavy ion reduces to the familiar reduced-mass two-body energy for one atom.

cards.numerical_form: Sample one steady ion velocity and two independent 700-nK Li velocities, remove the three-body COM motion, and average rate/spectrum values reproducibly.
open_questions: The author sample count, random seeds, and exact MD distributions are withheld.

cards.title: Threshold laws, peak regimes, and survival

source_refs.value: Quantum recombination model scaling discussion and experimental methods

cards.latex: \gamma_l\propto k^{2l}\;(\Gamma\ll\mathcal Kn),\quad k^{-1}\;(\Gamma=\Gamma_m),\quad k^{-2(l+1)}\;(\Gamma\gg\mathcal Kn),\qquad P_{\rm surv}=e^{-\langle\gamma_l\rangle t}

checks.reason: All three asymptotic laws are stated in the main text and exponential survival is stated in the methods.
Substitution of C_l^-2 proportional to k^(2l+1), v proportional to k, and the dominant denominator term yields the three printed powers.
Nonnegative rates produce survival in [0,1] and peak loss at an intermediate energy for higher l.

cards.numerical_form: Use asymptotic log-slope tests and probability bounds as machine acceptance for every model branch.

cards.title: Printed higher-partial-wave resonance-position trend

source_refs.value: Main Fig. 6(h), caption, and higher-partial-wave text

cards.latex: B_{\rm fit}(x)=B_*+[4.4(4)\,{\rm mG}/{\mu\rm K}](195\,{\mu\rm K})x,\quad x=\Delta E_{\rm ion}/\Delta E_{s,\rm ion}

checks.reason: The caption and text print the 4.4(4) mG/microkelvin slope, the seven normalized energies, and position anchors near 320.41, 320.59, and 321.53 G.
Slope times the effective-temperature energy axis produces a magnetic-field shift.
Using B*=320.0 G gives 321.55 G at x=1.81, consistent with the printed 321.53(3) G anchor without reading pixels.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate the printed linear slope on the seven declared x values; retain independently reconstructed quantum-model peak positions only as a diagnostic column.
open_questions: The fit intercept is not printed directly; 320.0 G is reconstructed from the textual anchors and is not paper-exact.
